name: ConsentLedger
purpose: Records granular per-subject, per-purpose consent grants and revocations with timestamp and version of the notice accepted.
api_signature:
from typing import Protocol
from datetime import datetime

class ConsentLedger(Protocol):
    def grant(self, subject_id: str, purpose: str, notice_version: str, at: datetime) -> str: ...
    def revoke(self, subject_id: str, purpose: str, at: datetime) -> None: ...
    def is_granted(self, subject_id: str, purpose: str, at: datetime | None = None) -> bool: ...
    def history(self, subject_id: str) -> list[dict]: ...
invariants: Consent MUST be keyed by (subject_id, purpose); a blanket grant across purposes CANNOT be recorded.
Every grant MUST reference a notice_version string so the exact text the subject accepted is reconstructible; missing version SHALL raise.
Revocation MUST be as easy as grant and SHALL take effect immediately; future is_granted calls for that (subject, purpose) MUST return False.
History entries MUST be append-only; a revocation NEVER erases a prior grant, it supersedes it in time.
is_granted MUST be evaluated against the state at `at` (or now), not the latest, so audits can reproduce past authorizations.
extension_contract: Target applications register purposes (e.g. 'marketing_email', 'analytics_profiling') and plug a NoticeVersionProvider adapter. Consent-gated code paths compose the ledger via a policy decorator that blocks execution when is_granted is False.

sources.locator: Article 7 Conditions for consent; Article 6(1)(a) lawful basis

sources.source: AICPA SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria (2017, 2022 revision)
sources.locator: Privacy criteria P3.1 — consent collection and documentation

why_essential: Consent scattered in flags or CRM fields cannot prove lawful basis at a point in time; a shared ledger keeps every grant reproducible and every revocation effective in one place.
alternatives_considered: Boolean column on users table — no history, no notice version, no temporal query.
CRM tool as source of truth — outside the transactional boundary, racy against data processing.
Cookie banner state only — covers web UI consent, not API/backend-initiated processing.
